skill.name: programmatic-seo
skill.description: When the user wants to create SEO-driven pages at scale using templates and data. Also use when the user mentions "programmatic SEO," "template pages," "pages at scale," "directory pages," "location pages," "[keyword] + [city] pages," "comparison pages," "integration pages," "building many pages for SEO," "pSEO," "generate 100 pages," "data-driven pages," or "templated landing pages." Use this whenever someone wants to create many similar pages targeting different keywords or locations. For auditing existing SEO issues, see seo-audit. For content strategy planning, see content-strategy.
skill.summary: Plans useful, scalable SEO pages with data-driven templates, internal linking, indexation controls, and quality checks.

content.user_title: Plan Programmatic SEO Pages at Scale
content.value_statement: Scaled SEO pages often become thin, repetitive, or difficult to index. This skill develops data-backed templates, linking plans, and quality controls for useful pages.
actual_capabilities: Selects among 12 programmatic SEO playbooks based on product assets, audience, and search intent.
Defines repeating keyword patterns, page variables, data requirements, and opportunity size.
Plans page templates with unique content, relevant calls to action, metadata, and structured data.
Designs hub, spoke, breadcrumb, sitemap, and related-page linking structures.
Creates launch checks for content quality, crawlability, indexation, and search intent.
Diagnoses common strategy-level indexation problems involving thin content, internal links, sitemaps, and crawl budget.
limitations: It does not collect live search volumes, rankings, or competitor data automatically.
It does not generate, deploy, or publish production pages.
Recommendations depend on accurate product, audience, keyword, and data-source inputs.
Full technical crawl audits and detailed 404 diagnosis require a dedicated SEO audit workflow.

use_cases.title: Scale Industry Landing Pages
use_cases.description: Plan distinct product pages for each industry with relevant workflows, proof, messaging, and internal links.

use_cases.title: Build a Search Directory
use_cases.description: Design data requirements, filters, URL patterns, page templates, and indexation priorities for a useful directory.

use_cases.title: Launch a Topic Glossary
use_cases.description: Structure definition pages, related-term links, category navigation, quality standards, and a prioritized publishing sequence.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Playbook
prompt_templates.prompt: I sell [product] to [audience]. Recommend the best programmatic SEO playbook for [search opportunity]. Explain the required data and unique page value.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner selection of a suitable page pattern

prompt_templates.title: Design a Page Template
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a template for [keyword pattern] pages. Include URL, title, headings, unique data sections, calls to action, related links, and quality criteria.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate planning for one scalable page type

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Scaled Launch
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a launch for [page count] pages using [data source]. Prioritize demand, define indexation stages, map internal links, and provide launch checks.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose Indexation
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this programmatic SEO setup: [details]. Diagnose low indexation using uniqueness, crawlability, internal linking, sitemaps, duplication, and crawl budget. Prioritize corrective actions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced strategic diagnosis of an existing page set

output_examples.output: Use the Personas playbook. Give each industry page distinct workflows, proof, features, terminology, and links from a central industry hub.
First compare indexed and excluded pages for uniqueness. Strengthen local data and internal links, remove weak variants, and submit segmented sitemaps.
Use an integration hub and individual pages with setup steps, supported workflows, screenshots, limitations, and related integrations.

best_practices: Provide specific, defensible value on every page instead of changing only template variables.
Prioritize page patterns with verified demand and reliable data before expanding the page count.
Connect every page through hubs, related links, breadcrumbs, and segmented sitemaps.
anti_patterns: Do not publish thousands of pages before validating search demand and page quality.
Do not use stale, scraped, or weakly licensed data without verification and update plans.
Do not create doorway pages, duplicate copy, keyword stuffing, or pages that serve only search engines.

faq.question: What is programmatic SEO?
faq.answer: Programmatic SEO creates many useful search pages from structured data and repeatable templates while preserving distinct value for each page.

faq.question: Does this skill write every page?
faq.answer: No. It plans opportunities, templates, data needs, linking, indexation, and quality checks. Production writing and publishing require separate workflows.

faq.question: Which page patterns are supported?
faq.answer: It covers templates, curation, conversions, comparisons, examples, locations, personas, integrations, glossaries, translations, directories, and profiles.

faq.question: Can it perform keyword research?
faq.answer: It structures keyword patterns and evaluation criteria. It needs supplied search volume, trend, and competition data for evidence-based prioritization.

faq.question: How does it reduce thin content risk?
faq.answer: It requires unique data, analysis, intent alignment, conditional sections, and useful page-specific details before recommending indexation.

faq.question: Can it audit technical SEO problems?
faq.answer: It can identify strategy-level indexation concerns. Detailed crawl errors, server responses, and technical audits need a dedicated SEO audit tool.
